ratings.reason: A clean browser-extension attachment: the host webpage remains intact while sentence-level highlights are injected at identifiable spans. The mechanism is directly rebuildable; impact is plausible but not demonstrated by the limited evidence.

Exceptionally clear combination of a pre-existing webpage, a global overview layer, and paragraph-anchored local annotations. The global/local grounding pattern transfers readily to many reading and inspection tasks.

Explicitly extends Notion through a Chrome extension, detects host content and focus, and places a widget beside the document. It is highly rebuildable, though a context-aware side widget is comparatively conventional.

The Google Docs add-on and sidebar establish the two separable layers unambiguously. The placement is easy to reproduce but is a standard host-panel move, and the quote does not describe the sidebar's interactions or resulting outcomes.

Text annotations overlaying a document and an accompanying chart suggest a detachable layer anchored to host content. However, the quote does not establish a third-party host application or explain how annotations map to paragraph spans, so scores are conservative.

A browser extension dynamically injects components into existing video platforms, directly matching the structural signature. Exact components and anchor locations are omitted, limiting rebuildability slightly, but the integration mechanism is strong.

The VS Code plugin places a chatbot beside the editor while preserving the programming environment. It is clear and broadly transferable, but a docked assistant beside an editor is the obvious baseline implementation.

An augmented note with phrase-level support weakly suggests an added layer anchored to an existing artifact. The evidence does not identify a host application, attachment point, separability, or visible interaction, so this is difficult to rebuild or confidently classify.

Embedding generated insights and cues directly within existing webpages is a central, highly transferable instance of the pattern. The precise forms and anchor-selection rules are absent, keeping mechanism clarity below exemplary.

The custom Premiere Pro extension and Assistant panel cleanly establish a detachable AI layer inside a mature host workflow. The placement is concrete but conventional, and the quote does not explain how panel output connects to transcript-editing stages.

Word-scale visualizations imply generated elements anchored at precise locations in pre-existing documents. This is interesting and transferable, but the quote omits the host surface, user action, and rendering behavior needed for a complete rebuild.

The browser plug-in combines a cross-page intent view with highlighting anchored to relevant webpage content. Both layers and their relationship are explicit, yielding a strong, rebuildable exemplar beyond its information-foraging domain.

A VS Code extension integrates generated narratives and captured activity directly with code, making the host and added layer explicit. Fine-grained code anchoring is distinctive, although the exact on-screen presentation is not specified.

The assistant occupies a task pane beside an intact spreadsheet, a clear and transferable host-panel arrangement. The paper intentionally follows the familiar Excel Copilot layout, making the move conventional; outcome claims are unavailable here.

The Chrome extension explicitly layers atop the independently usable ChatGPT website. The separability is unusually clear, though the quote does not identify specific host anchors or describe the generated layer's visible components.

Triggering suggestions at named stages of an existing code-iteration workflow fits stage-anchored injection. However, the quote does not identify the host surface, visible component, trigger conditions, or response interaction, making reconstruction difficult.

A Chrome extension appears as a floating window within Hookpad, clearly preserving the host while adding a separable generative surface. The attachment is broadly reusable, but the quote does not show content-level anchoring or detailed interaction.

The optional support mode injects a comparison entry point at a specific location in a live-commerce room. This is a concrete workflow attachment with plausible behavioral impact, though the subsequent generated panel and host relationship are not described.

The quote clearly advocates in-page adaptation rather than a separate destination, aligning conceptually with the pattern. It reads as a design principle rather than a specified interface, leaving attachment points and interaction behavior unjudgeable.

The system preserves Scratch's original GUI while incorporating a specialized assistant, supporting two separable layers. The quote does not state where the assistant is placed or how its steps attach to blocks, reducing mechanism clarity.

Colored scrollbar alerts and a point-of-entry icon are highly concrete host attachment points for augmenting privacy-policy reading. The title supplies the broader host context, but the quote alone does not explicitly establish the extension architecture or generated content.

Visual highlights anchored to existing UI elements form a detachable guidance layer over smartphone applications. The mechanism is concrete, but the quoted evidence does not specify how the layer is technically attached or what the chatbot generates.

The quote explicitly distinguishes FigJam's retained graph interface from a plugin adding generative and conversion features. This is a strong, portable plugin architecture, though the particular insertion points and on-screen responses remain underspecified.

A single new, named button inserts natural-language project generation into the established App Inventor platform. The attachment point is exceptionally rebuildable and transferable, but adding a generation button is not a particularly novel layout move.

Deploying generated scaffold interfaces inside Blender strongly suggests an AI layer fitted to a complex host application. The adaptive scaffolding is unusually interesting, but the evidence supplies no placement, controls, anchoring rules, or user interaction sequence.

The Figma plugin consumes host designs and heuristics and renders generated feedback, a clear plugin-to-artifact relationship. The quote is truncated before explaining where or how feedback is rendered, so the core attachment mechanism is only partially rebuildable.

Integrating LLM-supported components into an existing scholarly infrastructure directly expresses the pattern and is broadly transferable. The description remains at intent and architecture level, without concrete components, host anchors, or interaction behavior.

SnapClass is visibly integrated into an independently useful programming environment and keeps grading inside that host workflow. The quote does not establish a separable plugin layer, identifiable anchor, or specifically generated content, so fit is only moderate.

In-situ explanations suggest content-level anchoring, but the quote only calls Ivie an extension to a programming assistant. It does not identify the independently authored host artifact, placement, user action, or rendering mechanism; the title alone cannot fill those gaps.

A Figma plugin adds LLM behavior to mock-ups while leaving the mature design host intact, cleanly matching the pattern. It is broadly transferable and interesting, but the quote does not explain the plugin's visible surface or attachment to particular mock-up elements.
